input.quote: 13.5 Liquidated Damages. Customer acknowledges that M&I shall suffer a material adverse impact on its business if this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A) and that the resulting damages may not be susceptible of precise determination. Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
input.rationale: Section 13.5 expressly characterises two Customer-payable fees as liquidated damages, and each is quantified as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value (remaining-term value) under Sections 11.1 and 11.2(A), with the Termination for Cause Fee triggered by any Event of Default. That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) and approaches walk-away territory. Deleting the fees outright would require collateral rewrites of the exit mechanics, so we take the fallback: we cap the early-termination fee at three months of Fees in 11.1, fold 11.2(A) into that same fee rather than a separate remaining-value fee, and confirm in 13.5 that it is the only liquidated amount we pay. Exit notice and payment mechanics are left to T4C.

proposal.summary: Cap the early-termination fee at three months' Fees, remove the separate Termination for Cause Fee, and make that fee the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the remaining-term percentage penalty with our accepted three-month cap, removed the separate Termination for Cause Fee, and confirmed that this early-termination fee is the only liquidated amount payable by us.
